items.summary: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Austin gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Nov 6. Sales have been weak: Kelley Blue Book reported just 20,237 Cybertrucks sold in the United States in 2025, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, against a pre-launch prediction of 250,000 units. The wind-down would free capacity for the newly launched Cybercab model central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions.
items.title: Tesla winds down Cybertruck production for robotaxi pivot

items.summary:
Global investors are pressing South Korean conglomerates to speed up corporate governance reforms, but progress has been uneven. Samsung Electronics illustrates the resistance: it reported record quarterly operating profit yet trades at 1.87 times book value versus Nvidia's 29 and Apple's 44. Activist Life Asset Management asked Samsung to review its decision to defer deploying remaining shareholder-return funds until January, while Palliser Capital called for buybacks at Samsung and Hyundai Motor. Banks have largely complied with reforms, but large chaebol affiliates are resisting as their lobbying intensifies, raising concerns the momentum behind President Lee Jae Myung's drive could stall.

visual null
items.title: Samsung Resists Corporate Reforms as Investors Push Back on South Korea's Biggest Chaebol

items.summary: Elon Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production next year, though he did not say whether it fully stops or moves elsewhere. Lead engineer Wes Morrill suggested the vehicle is being discontinued, living on through the self-driving Cybercab. Fans mourn online; critics and recalls weighed in earlier.
items.title: Musk Signals Cybertruck Production Wind-Down at Texas Factory

items.summary: RW-Voice EQ AS announces a collaboration with Liva AI to add private data covering two new accents, Egyptian and Nigerian English, to the Open ASR Leaderboard. The additions follow earlier splits from Appen and DataOceanAI and Voice Arena. RW-Voice frames the work as part of an effort to improve accent representation in speech-recognition evaluations and reduce benchmark gaming, noting that more accents allow a richer breakdown based on Kachru’s Three Circles model.
items.title: Liva AI Partners to Add Egyptian and Nigerian Accents to Open ASR Leaderboard

items.summary: After researcher Mrinank Sharma resigned from Anthropic and posted a widely viewed letter warning of an “in peril” world, white-collar professionals across tech, public relations, consulting and other fields say AI has altered their work. Some have left entirely for careers such as teaching, policing or acting; others pursue additional degrees or freelance streams to feel more secure. Economic data from the Economist shows AI created about 1m US jobs versus 200,000 layoffs attributed to it, yet a Pew Research Center survey found 71% of Americans expect fewer jobs over 20 years. University of Notre Dame economics professor Brendan Moore says fears may stem more from tech leaders’ warnings than from data, though he warns mass resignations could still affect wages and growth.
items.title: White-collar workers quit jobs amid AI fears

items.summary: Tesla raised US Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and stopped accepting orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim, making the cheapest orderable model $92,490. The move follows Tesla's confirmation it will end production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027. This is the second price increase in under three months; Premium AWD prices rose 15.6% since early August and entry prices jumped 32%. Analysts say higher prices on a truck with falling demand signal a wind-down, pushing buyers toward higher-margin trims before production ends around mid-2027.
items.title: Tesla Raises Cybertruck Prices Before Ending Production

items.summary: Tesla is ending Cybertruck production, with CEO Elon Musk announcing Friday that the automaker will wind down the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027. Tesla says it wants to free capacity for more Cybercab output, though analysts note Giga Texas has ample idle space and Cybercab volumes are low. The truck sells at roughly a tenth of its planned 250,000-unit annual line, with estimated deliveries near 30,000 units a year versus installed capacity above 125,000. Tesla does not break out Cybertruck sales separately, lumping them into Other Models, which fell 48% in Q3 2026 to 8,295 units. The item notes no details yet on inventory or owner service plans.
items.title: Tesla Ends Cybertruck Production Citing Weak Sales

items.summary: Japan's population is falling, especially in rural areas, yet abandoned farms are also losing wildlife rather than gaining it. A 2025 study from Japan found biodiversity stayed stable only where the human population did; elsewhere butterflies, fireflies, frogs, birds and native plants declined. Nature reports that humans had shaped these mosaic landscapes for species to depend on. Adam Spitzig of Stanford University said small farms can boost biodiversity while supporting food production.
items.title: Abandoned Japanese Farms Lose Wildlife as Villages Empty

items.summary: A bipartisan permitting reform bill, BAAJA, faces uncertainty after Democrats won midterm control of Congress. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries opposed the legislation in its current form, citing concerns it revises laws like the National Environmental Policy Act and weakens environmental statutes. Lobbyist Chris Moyer said Democratic leverage has changed his outlook on passing it during the lame-duck session. Analyst Kevin Kircher's report found the bill would raise clean electricity revenue by $2.1 million per life lost to pollution from fossil fuels, below the EPA's roughly $12 million standard. Clean energy groups urge swift passage before Congress ends this year while business and environmental advocates debate trade-offs over accelerating both renewable and fossil fuel projects.
items.title: Democratic Gains Cast Doubt on Energy Permitting Bill

items.summary: Nearly 50 residents gathered in Fairfax, Iowa, to voice anger and fear over a proposed natural gas plant less than three miles from town. Nine months earlier, Interstate Power and Light had abandoned plans after opposition; Alliant Energy then announced land purchase for the site. In October, the Linn County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to reject Alliant's rezoning request, citing water infrastructure gaps and overwhelming community opposition. The Morgan Valley Energy Center would run 1,230 to 3,950 hours yearly. Residents link rising demand from nearby data centers—Google and QTS campuses using combined 1.6 gigawatts—to the need for fossil plants, raising concerns amid Linn County's net-zero goal by 2050 set in 2019. Alliant disputed the rejection; a utilities commission hearing is scheduled next month.
items.title: Iowa Residents Reject Gas Plant Amid Data Center Growth

items.summary: The European Commission charged TikTok on Friday with failing to protect users’ mental health, saying its algorithm can be harmful and leads vulnerable young people down rabbit holes they cannot easily escape. The preliminary finding under the Digital Services Act says safeguards against repetitive content are ineffective. TikTok called the findings false and meritless and said it would challenge them; officials could fine it up to 6% of global turnover.
items.title: EU Charges TikTok Over Harmful Mental Health Content

items.summary: On November 6, Amazon announced that US customers could use its AI-powered assistant, Alexa for Shopping, to search and buy products through text messages. The feature lets users research items, compare prices, track deals, and complete purchases on their behalf. It is rolling out first to a small group of invited customers before a broader launch in the coming weeks.
items.title: Amazon Expands Alexa for Shopping via Text Messages

items.summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory by mid-2026 to free the plant for the Cybercab self-driving taxi. The move ends a struggling launch, with deliveries of only 8,300 trucks in one quarter against an aim of 200,000 yearly. Musk has instead bet on robotics and artificial intelligence.
items.title: Musk shifts Tesla focus away from Cybertruck toward robots and AI

items.summary: Protesters broke into a construction site for a Microsoft AI data centre in Amsterdam on Friday, opening two days of rallies across 16 countries. The Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition backs the actions calling to pause large-scale construction over resource and climate concerns. Pure Data Centres plans more than $1 billion investment and urged protesters to leave safely. EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said Europe needs data centres but with care, warning of rising energy bills and environmental damage.
items.title: Activists Breach Microsoft Data Centre Site Amid Europe-Wide Protests

items.summary: AI company Anthropic introduced a new Personal Finance feature in its chatbot Claude, helping users track bank and credit card spending. The beta is available only in the United States for Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Personal Finance Feature to Claude AI Chatbot

items.summary: A half-day career guidance workshop built around a personalised app raised high school enrolment and completion among grade 9 students in rural Cambodia, with gains lasting more than three years. The study randomly assigned schools to treatment or control groups (Gehrke, Lenel, and Schupp forthcoming), following 1,715 students through official records plus a phone survey conducted about five months after the workshop during COVID-19 lockdowns. Treated students scored higher on their grade 9 final exam and were more likely to enrol in high school, progress further, sit midterms, and complete secondary schooling roughly 3.5 years later. Gains concentrated among stronger students; weaker ones may have aligned aspirations with vocational routes. The authors note the workshop cost about US$7 per student and offer lessons for scaling guidance without reproducing inequalities.
items.title: Low-Cost Career Workshop Boosts High School Enrolment in Cambodia

items.summary: This week's VoxDevTalks episode highlights several studies in development economics, covering supply chains, economic inclusion, manufacturing and growth models. Researchers found that India's COVID-era supply chains held up when built on complex inputs; Ugandan people with disabilities participate 18–20% less in economic activity despite an inclusive programme improving their livelihoods but not community attitudes; most Indian manufacturing workers are in small firms, explaining around 40% of the firm-size gap between poorer and richer states; and a career guidance workshop raised high school enrolment in rural Cambodia for over three years. Tim Besley discusses state capacity clusters, while Michael Peters examines service-led growth.
items.title: This week in development economics at VoxDev: 06/11/2026

items.summary: Anthropic faces lower initial public offering valuations following a steep AI-stock decline, with prospective buyers discussing $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, according to Bloomberg. Some investors previously cited up to $2 trillion in early October. The Nasdaq fell 6.4% on Thursday, erasing $2.3 trillion of market capitalization and setting a one-session record. Anthropic's amended Form S-1 reported $33.24 billion revenue for January through September with a net loss; its last funding round valued it at $965 billion.
items.title: Anthropic IPO valuation expectations fall after AI stock selloff

items.summary: IT services company Coforge entered a strategic partnership with SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI), joining its Partner Network as a Transformation Partner. The collaboration focuses on helping businesses integrate and deploy the Grok portfolio across enterprise operations, with solutions tailored to individual requirements and designed to deliver measurable outcomes.
items.title: Coforge Joins SpaceX Super Intelligence Network for Grok AI Deployment

items.summary: CEO Elon Musk said Tesla will phase out Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to expand Cybercab output. He stated the truck sold 70,000 units over three years with a net project loss of $1.9 billion against $2 billion in research and development spending. The move reflects Tesla's broader shift toward artificial intelligence and robotics as it axed other models this year.
items.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production for Cybercab Expansion

items.summary: The U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, according to a Labor Department report released Friday. The job market picked up steam last month while the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1% from 4.2% the previous month. Industries adding jobs included health care, manufacturing, and business services, while restaurants and construction cut positions. Average wages rose 3.1% year over year, though an Indeed economist said workers remain losing ground as inflation climbed to 3.7% in September.
items.title: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October as unemployment fell

items.summary: The Indicator from Planet Money reports that gold dropped below $4,000 per ounce this week after reaching nearly $5,600 in January. Co-host Jeff Guo says the main driver is rising Treasury bond yields, which offer income and act as an inflation hedge—advantages gold lacks since it earns no interest. While geopolitical tension from the Iran war could push investors toward safe havens, its effect so far has mainly raised oil prices, pushing rates up and making bonds more attractive than gold. The newsletter notes economic uncertainty remains but does not attribute a single cause definitively to one factor beyond yields.
items.title: Indicator explains why gold prices fell below $4,000

items.summary: Brussels warned TikTok on Friday that it must change the design of its personalised For You feed or risk large fines under the Digital Services Act, after finding preliminary evidence of violations. The European Commission said the algorithm's 'rabbit hole' effect repeatedly recommends similar content, potentially exposing children to harmful material about sadness and body image. TikTok rejected the findings as fundamentally inaccurate, saying they misrepresent how its platform works while maintaining a strong record of protecting users.
items.title: EU Orders TikTok To Overhaul For You Feed Amid Child Safety Concerns

items.summary: The European Commission said in preliminary findings that TikTok's recommendation algorithm may repeatedly expose users, especially minors and vulnerable adults, to harmful content such as videos on mental health struggles, weight loss and body image. The bloc found TikTok failed to adequately assess or mitigate these risks. If confirmed, the commission could impose a fine of up to 6% of TikTok's global annual turnover under Digital Services Act proceedings.
items.title: EU Flags TikTok's Feed as Risk of Harmful Content

items.summary: Parents of a 13-year-old girl sued Google in California, alleging she used the company's AI-powered search on a school-issued Chromebook to plan her suicide. Filed Monday 2 November, it is believed to be the first such negligence claim over school-blocked AI features. The complaint says Emma had no mental illness history before entering a psychological crisis after using the engine. Google says its AI Mode includes self-harm safeguards and is reviewing the claims; attorney Andrew Liddell urged schools to keep search off until safety measures improve.
items.title: Parents Sue Google Over AI Search and a Teen's Suicide

items.summary: The Hong Kong High Court sentenced Joshua Wong Chi-fung on November 5, 2026 to a 10-year prison term for conspiring with foreign forces under the National Security Law. The ruling treats his conduct as one continuing offense spanning multiple acts aimed at endangering national security. Earlier convictions include an 56-month sentence in November 2024 for conspiracy to subvert state power, and involvement in the 2019 protests against extradition amendments. Author Kong Qingjiang of CGTN argues that freedom must operate within legal boundaries and warns that those who threaten national security face accountability as Hong Kong moves toward stability.
items.title: Hong Kong Court Sentences Joshua Wong To Ten Years

items.summary: Xiamen's World Ocean Week offered the public a rare chance to climb inside a full-scale simulator of China's Jiaolong manned submersible. The event featured CGTN's Liu Jiaxin, who took a simulated dive with a real pilot to experience 7,000-meter pressure firsthand. Jiaolong is China's first operational deep-sea manned submersible, designed for depths up to 7,000 meters.
items.title: Public Simulated Dive Inside China's Jiaolong Submersible

items.summary: The article presents Xiamen, called the "Garden City" in Southeast China, as a place known for beautiful seascapes and green spaces where wildlife thrive. It describes how the city has developed its ecological reputation over decades of consistent environmental action, then invites readers to explore what it calls an inspiring story about the region's natural beauty and long-standing commitment to protecting it.
items.title: Xiamen Showcases Its Green City Legacy Through Environmental Storytelling

items.summary: China's top legislature adopted a law on Friday to prevent and punish cross-border corruption. Passed at a session of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, it aims to deepen international anti-corruption cooperation while safeguarding China's sovereignty, security and development interests. The law contains 47 articles across six chapters covering mechanisms, case handling and legal liability.
items.title: China Adopts Law Against Cross-Border Corruption

items.summary: Chinese scientists cooled a cloud of rubidium atoms aboard China's space station to an equivalent temperature of 9.7 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero, described by the research team as a record low. The findings were published in Science and used the ultracold atom physics facility in the Mengtian laboratory module. Researchers observed the cloud expansion for seven seconds after release, which could support quantum experiments and precision measurements. Wolfgang Ketterle noted that on Earth the cloud would fall about 250 meters before crashing to the ground.
items.title: Chinese Team Sets Atomic Cooling Record on Space Station

items.summary: A Macao court sentenced former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San, 69, to 12½ years in prison Friday in the region's first national security case after a closed-door trial. He was found guilty of subverting state power, breaching confidentiality and contacting overseas groups between 2023 and 2024, including leaking confidential gaming-license information as a lawmaker in 2021. The secrecy drew concerns about fairness from critics like Portuguese lawyer Jorge Menezes, who said Au did not plead guilty. His wife Virginia Cheang called it groundless persecution, while the Macao government backed the ruling and urged respect for national security law enforcement.
items.title: Macao Sentences Ex-Lawmaker in First National Security Case

items.summary: A Kenyan court sentenced doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie to a total of 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one children. Justice Diana Mochache found him guilty after ruling he bore the primary criminal culpability for instructing followers to fast to death so they could meet Jesus. Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, which she declined despite meeting its threshold, citing no prospect of rehabilitation. Mackenzie was tried with 28 accomplices who received sentences up to 160 years. The convictions cover only 191 victims while more than 400 bodies were exhumed from Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast.
items.title: Kenyan Court Sentences Doomsday Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie to Life

items.summary: Czech arms maker Czechoslovak Group (CSG) announced in mid-October that it has acquired a stake in Canadian space technology manufacturer MDA Space. The deal is part of the company's bid to continue riding the defense boom driven by Russia's war in Ukraine, which expanded CZ sector exports from €600 million in 2021 to €4.7 billion in 2025. CSG estimates global government spending on space defense reached €65.83 billion last year and that the overall space economy will triple to €1.6 trillion over the next decade, though it frames these as company estimates.
items.title: Czech CSG Buys Space Tech Firm Amid Arms Boom

items.summary: A federal judge has temporarily blocked construction of President Trump's 250-foot arch in Washington, D.C., with District Court Judge Tanya Chutkan halting work for 14 days at the request of D.C. and Virginia governments. NPR's Rachel Treisman reports that a National Capital Planning Commission filled with Trump allies approved the project despite significant opposition. Separately, the Labor Department is set to release its latest jobs report; NPR's Scott Horsley says it may show employers added about 60,000 jobs last month. The newsletter also covers school enrollment declines and health claims about fluoride alternatives.
items.title: Judge Halts Trump's Arch; Labor Department Set to Release Jobs Report

items.summary: Many Zambians seek civil service careers for its stability, but recent retirements, dismissals and restructuring across public institutions have unsettled that perception. Affected staff include former police officer Godfrey Chilabi, dismissed in October; deputy inspector general Charity Munganga; and all Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency workers following an audit reset. ZEMA directors were placed on administrative leave pending assessment. The changes sparked parliamentary debate after the August 2026 election, with opposition lawmakers led by Stephen Kampyongo questioning transparency amid high living costs.
items.title: Zambia's Civil Service Overhaul Raises Questions About Fairness and Transparency

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV departed Friday for his first trip to the Americas since being elected in May 2025, traveling through November 17. He will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru but not the United States, declining a White House invitation tied to the July 4 Declaration of Independence anniversary. The itinerary emphasizes coexistence and unity amid regional polarization, though his message on social justice may clash with governments aligned with President Trump. His health is under scrutiny after lung-tumor surgery in October; Vatican sources say he needs no special measures. Heavy El Niño rains have triggered emergencies across northern Peru ahead of large gatherings.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV's First Americas Trip Under Trump's Shadow

items.summary: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck off the coast of Tokyo on Friday, Japanese authorities said, with no tsunami alert issued. The shallow quake hit at 7:39 pm near Kanto region, and Japan's Meteorological Agency reported seismic intensity 3, meaning almost everyone indoors felt shaking and dishes may rattle. Its epicenter lay about 169 kilometers southeast of Asahi per the US Geological Survey. There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries.
items.title: Magnitude 6.1 Quake Strikes Near Tokyo Without Tsunami Warning

items.summary: In the midterm elections, voters under 30 showed the sharpest shift toward the Democrats after many had backed Donald Trump in 2024. About seven in ten young voters supported the Democratic candidate for Congress, and roughly six in ten cited opposition to Trump as a reason. The swing was largest among Latino youth, who voted overwhelmingly Democratic, while older groups moved less sharply.
items.title: Young Voters Drove Democratic Midterm Gains

items.summary: Japan convened its first government panel of experts Friday to help draft a plan reversing the country’s declining birthrate and restructuring systems for a shrinking population. Minister Minoru Kiuchi called it “a national crisis that is unfolding quietly.” Japan’s fertility rate was 1.14 last year, the lowest on record, while deaths (766,746) outpaced births (320,458). IPSS projections put the population below 100 million by 2056 and as low as about 80 million by 2070. The panel’s views will inform a strategy due by December.
items.title: Japan convenes expert panel on population decline

items.summary: A wave of student and cost-of-living protests has spread from France to Belgium, Germany, Italy, Spain and Portugal. Some marches turned violent with clashes, looting and destruction, while authorities faced criticism for excessive force and mass arrests. The unrest comes against mounting economic pressure: France's public debt is projected to reach 120 percent of GDP by 2027, and inflation across the EU and eurozone hit 3.8 percent in September, up from 2.1 percent in 2024.
items.title: Student and cost-of-living protests spread across Europe amid economic strain

items.summary: Jean-Luc Melenchon, a hard-left candidate in the upcoming 2027 French presidential election, is popular with young voters but also highly controversial. His support for youth protests has increased his divisiveness ahead of the vote. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young supporters to explore why he remains favored by Gen Z.
items.title: Why Jean-Luc Melenchon Appeals to French Gen Z Voters

items.summary: Goldman Sachs limited access to Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft GitHub to engineers, per October internal guidance seen by Bloomberg. Traders and bankers who used these tools for months lost them after a productivity and risk review. Spokesperson Nick Carcaterra said the firm offers AI tools during trials before handing them to best-suited staff. The move reverses July praise from CIO Marco Argenti for traders' 'vibe coding.' Goldman still built an in-house assistant combining OpenAI, Anthropic, and Alphabet models.
items.title: Goldman Sachs Restricts AI Coding Tools to Engineers and Strats

items.summary: Tribal leader Nisha Kumari Bhagat was found dead at her Ranchi residence on Friday, hours after allegedly going live on Facebook. Police suspect suicide but say circumstances remain unestablished. In the nearly 11-minute video, she cried and alleged that speaking out against the Hemant Soren government meant inviting death. Opposition leader Babulal Marandi expressed grief, alleging harassment for defending tribal rights, and called for chief minister Hemant Soren to resign.
items.title: Jharkhand tribal leader dies by suicide after Facebook Live post

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Anthropic faces investor resistance over its proposed $1.5 trillion initial public offering, following a sharp decline in US technology stocks. Three prospective investors want the valuation lowered; one suggested about $1 trillion and another cut the target to around $80 billion. Company executives are expected to review plans shortly, with no final decisions announced.
items.title: Anthropic IPO Valuation Meets Investor Resistance Amid Tech Selloff

items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a model designed to find and exploit security flaws, to vetted Daybreak Red customers on Thursday, rating it 'Critical' under its safety framework. OpenAI said the model helped identify 81 previously unknown Firefox vulnerabilities that Mozilla classified as high severity and built exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including 588 previously unknown ones, plus disclosed 304 critical Linux findings to maintainers. The company cited rising attempts by malicious cyber actors to misuse AI.
items.title: OpenAI Rates GPT-6 Cyber as Critical for Security

items.summary: Three House Republican committee chairs asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to brief them behind closed doors on his reported relationship with Alice Huang, an executive accused of passing information to Chinese intelligence. The letter requests a November 18 meeting before Nvidia's third-quarter earnings report. Trump was reportedly briefed but took no action. Megaspeed and Nvidia say the interactions were not unusual and allege no wrongdoing.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Asked To Brief Congress Over Alleged China Ties

items.summary: India's IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the government's semiconductor and manufacturing schemes will prioritise serious, technologically capable players with long-term commitments. Coinciding with the Friday launch of the Semicon 2.0 web application portal for machines, fabs and packaging applications, he asked the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme Secretary to reject about 18-19 non-serious applicants already identified. He said only complete applications from value-focused players aligned with Atmanirbhar Bharat would be accepted.
items.title: IT Minister Vaishnaw Demands Long-Term Commitment From Semiconductor Players

items.summary: The Election Commission announced on Friday that voters excluded from draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision exercise in seven states—Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland—will get another opportunity to be included in final rolls. Those marked Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate need not submit Form-8 if they have moved residence; instead they should submit an enumeration form with Annexure-C stating the new address. Officials will also set up a monitoring mechanism to prevent both denial and duplicate enrolments.
items.title: Election Commission Offers Second Chance for Excluded Voters

items.summary: On Dhanteras, Indian jewellery and metal stocks rose amid improving market sentiment, with Titan Company rebounding 3. 5% from its day's low while Kalyan Jewellers gained 5%. The rally follows strong earnings by Titan and a second consecutive session of gains for the Sensex and Nifty. Axis Securities notes gold has corrected more than 20% from its peak, setting an upside target of Rs 1,50,000 per 10 grams with support at Rs 1,21,000; Religare Broking recommends accumulation in silver within the Rs 1,50,000-Rs 1,63,000 per kg range.
items.title: Dhanteras lifts gold stocks as brokers see value in correction

items.summary: The Indian stock market will hold a one-hour Muhurat Trading session on Sunday from 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm, with the pre-open period running earlier. The exchanges detailed order-entry windows, limit-order rules and closing auctions across that window. MCX’s special commodity session runs separately until 2:19 pm. The market will next close on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada. Article writer Debaroti Adhikary is not a SEBI-registered analyst or adviser, and views are those of the original research report only.
items.title: Indian Exchanges Set Muhurat Trading and Diwali Closure Times for 2026

items.summary: Ravi Uppal, co-founder of the Mahadev betting app and one of its main promoters alongside Sourabh Chandrakar, was arrested in Dubai. The Enforcement Directorate and Central Bureau of Investigation are working to bring him back to India at the earliest, per news agency ANI. An Interpol Red Corner Notice had been issued against Uppal in October 2023; he was detained in December that year but released after 45 days. The ED alleges he oversaw a hawala network with transactions worth hundreds of crores and facilitated movement of funds into India, while also accusing him of links to Chhattisgarh politicians and bureaucrats. In January 2026 the agency attached assets worth approximately ₹21 crore linked to him. Both men reportedly hold Vanuatu passports used to evade Indian agencies; Vanuatu has no extradition treaty with India.
items.title: Mahadev App Co-Founder Ravi Uppal Arrested in Dubai on Hawala Charges

items.summary: The Election Commission said citizens whose names were dropped from draft electoral rolls during the special revision can submit a fresh enumeration form to be added to the final list. The rule applies where forms went missing or people were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate. Booth officers will issue new forms; movers must attach residence proof and need not file Form 8.
items.title: Election Commission lets excluded voters reapply in seven states and territories

items.summary: Kerala-born Nithya Raman won the Los Angeles mayoral race, becoming the first Indian-American and first South Asian elected to lead the city. Incumbent Karen Bass conceded defeat after her term was undermined by the Palisades Fire, making her the first LA mayor in two decades to lose reelection. Raman, an urban planner and Ivy League-educated council member since 2020, campaigned on housing, homelessness and policing reform. She entered as a late entrant who had initially backed Bass before flipping. Her victory means New York and Los Angeles will both have South Asian mayors. The Indian-American community registered broad midterm gains across the country.
items.title: Nithya Raman Wins Los Angeles Mayoral Race as First South Asian Mayor

items.summary: India Today Digital's ground check at Sadar Bazar found illegal and uncertified firecrackers on sale despite the Supreme Court allowing only certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR. The team observed questionable products, QR codes returning no information, China-made stock with Mandarin labels, and little understanding among sellers of what a green cracker is. Security personnel from Delhi Police, CRPF and CISF were present but seen buying rather than enforcing rules; one advised on transport instead of inspecting goods. A shopkeeper said buyers should rush purchases before police arrive. On Friday morning the city's AQI crossed 700 while enforcement appeared minimal. The Supreme Court order permits certified green crackers only on November 7 and 8 within set hours, but visible compliance was lacking.
items.title: Police Present But Unchecked at Delhi Cracker Market

items.summary: The Supreme Court permitted certified green crackers for Diwali in Delhi NCR on specific dates and times, with a total ban from November 9. Separately, India has improved cyclone disaster preparedness since the 1999 Odisha super cyclone through advanced forecasting models, Doppler radars, satellites, timely warnings enabling large-scale evacuations supported by shelters and coastal barriers. Despite effective emergency responses preventing human loss, challenges remain in restoring livelihoods, homes, and infrastructure after disasters.
items.title: India Strengthens Cyclone Preparedness Since 1999 Odisha Disaster

items.summary: Hindustan Times' evening news brief of November 6 leads with two stories. Delhi-NCR implemented Stage 3 of the Graded Response Action Plan (Grap) after its air quality index reached 382, classified as 'very poor', approaching the 400 mark that would trigger a 'severe' category; the restrictions target dust pollution and emissions across Noida, Ghaziabad and Gurugram. Separately, an FIR into Thursday's Chawri Bazar building collapse in Old Delhi, which killed at least two people, alleges contractors ignored worker warnings about poor construction material and structural weakness.
items.title: HT Evening News Brief November 6: Grap 3 imposed in Delhi, FIR on Chawri Bazar collapse reveals ignored warnings
